A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIRA research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original watermark-evasion experiments, text-quality measurements, ablations, runtime measurements, and additional dataset and SimMark evaluations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds longer-text, localized-detector, watermark-defense, and auxiliary-model evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions use surprisal-based token selection, a global suppression set, negative logit bias during rewriting, and adaptive bias relaxation upon degeneration. Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same procedures. Renaming the proxy green set and expanding its motivation do not change BIRA; context-adaptive biasing remains future work.

E1.justification: C4, Dolly CW, DBpedia, and the text-rewriting task are retained. v5 extends evaluation to longer inputs, localized detection through WinMax, PMARK, and watermark signals concentrated at low-entropy positions. These broaden the tested input and detection conditions without adding a new dataset, language, or application domain.

E2.justification: Vanilla, DIPPER-1, DIPPER-2, SIRA, and KGW-trained ADA remain in their corresponding attack comparisons. The new longer-text comparison reuses existing attack baselines. PMARK and WinMax extend the defended systems tested rather than introducing competing rewriting attacks.

E3.justification: The original 500-prompt, 230-token protocol is retained. New evaluations introduce 500 samples of 600-token Qwen2.5-32B outputs, maximum-span detection, entropy-gated watermarking and detection at 30th/50th-percentile thresholds, watermark-bias sweeps, and four auxiliary-model configurations. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Naming OPT-1.3B for the original experiment is additional disclosure, not evidence of a changed generator.

E4.justification: v5 adds robustness tests addressing longer-text rewriting, surviving localized watermark signals, low-entropy and stronger-bias defenses, and dependence on the auxiliary tokenizer/model (Section 5.3; Appendices E.3–E.5 and I). Existing bias/percentile ablations, random-token comparisons, detection-bound analysis, perplexity analysis, and ADA comparisons are retained or moved.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ± reporting for z-scores and runtime. The new auxiliary-model table provides analogous numerical summaries without specifying a new uncertainty estimator. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Retained per-method benchmark scores are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. On the new 600-token Qwen/SIR setting, Table 9 reports BIRA versus SIRA TPRs of 4.0% versus 20.8% at 1% FPR and LLM judgments of 4.14 versus 1.33. PMARK, WinMax, defense variants, and auxiliary-model findings are also added. Section 5.3 corrects v3 Appendix C's erroneous negative P90 summary to 0.075 for BIRA and 0.797 for Vanilla, matching the retained plot.

T1.justification: v3's explicit proxy-miss-rate assumptions, adjusted threshold, and supporting derivation in Section 4.2 and Appendix A.1 are removed. The central threshold-reduction result, exponential detection bound exp(-Nδ²/2), their proofs, and the sentence-level extension remain substantively unchanged. This is a limited deletion of subsidiary theoretical support.

C1.justification: Both versions' abstract, introduction, and conclusion center on the same theoretical characterization, query-free BIRA attack, high evasion with semantic preservation, and vulnerability of current watermarking methods. v5 clarifies the sufficient-condition framing and adds supporting evidence without introducing a different central contribution.

C2.justification: v5 develops a realized-watermark-trace explanation for the suppression set and replaces v3's SimMark embedding-shift explanation with sentence-segmentation disruption. It removes the explicit discussion of SIRA's higher SimMark ASR and worse fidelity despite retaining that table. New discussion interprets defense-quality tradeoffs, auxiliary-model stability, and limitations of uniform suppression in mixed natural-language/code contexts.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code repository link, identifies OPT-1.3B as the original watermark generator, and explicitly distinguishes generation from rewriting models. It also documents settings for the new entropy-gated, longer-text, and auxiliary-model experiments. Existing pseudocode, prompts, attack hyperparameters, degeneration settings, and hardware/runtime information remain available.

R1.justification: v5 adds references to Huo et al. on PMARK, Kuditipudi et al. on distortion-free watermarks, and Zhang et al. on OPT. It expands positioning around sentence-level robustness and stronger text generators while retaining the established query-based/query-free distinction and relationship to SIRA.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, theoretical exposition, and method motivation undergo extensive rewriting. Detection-bound analysis moves into Section 5.3, computational efficiency moves to an appendix, and the appendices are reorganized. Terminology changes to proxy suppression set, and acknowledgments, an impact statement, and a discussion section are added.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column conference layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. New tables present longer-text, defense, and auxiliary-model results; ASR tables lose their average columns. Existing plots are largely reused, while the overview labels and detection-bound annotations are revised.

improvement.justification: The new stress tests address practical robustness questions left untested in v3, and the generator disclosure and code link improve reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by narrower formal support after removal of the proxy-set argument and a less balanced SimMark discussion despite unchanged results. Overall, v5 strengthens empirical support and transparency, with a limited net improvement in paper quality.
